character_facts: Aghnar is a newborn infant on this page.
Aghnar has a visible or diagnosed problem affecting normal movement, especially walking or leg function.
The mother is protective and refuses to accept that her son is doomed.
The stern examiner considers physical normalcy essential for training.
The final speaker is confident enough to override the examiner and assume responsibility for Aghnar's training.
characters_present: Dark-haired woman holding the baby, likely his mother
Large stern man examining the child and judging his fitness
Shadowed final speaker who volunteers to train Aghnar
continuity_links: This page appears to mark Aghnar's origin point as a physically impaired heir whose future must be redefined through alternative training.
The threat that this is 'the end' of the Metabarons sets up a succession crisis resolved, for now, by the promise of Shabda-Oud training.
dialogue_meaning: One authority figure believes the baby's bodily condition means the Metabaron line is finished.
The mother rejects that judgment and argues the child still has potential.
The baby's leg or mobility problem is presented as serious enough to affect combat training.
A separate speaker resolves the dispute by personally taking charge of the child's martial education.
The page introduces the Shabda-Oud as a specialized or secret combat discipline.
locations: Interior setting, exact location not shown
lore_facts: The Metabarons are treated as a lineage whose continuation depends on the physical capability of heirs.
Aghnar is named on the page.
The Shabda-Oud is described as involving secret skills and combat training.
plot_events: An older or authoritative man declares that this is the end of the Metabarons, implying the newborn's condition threatens the lineage.
The mother protests and insists her son will be able to stand or walk, urging the man to look more closely.
A close inspection of the baby's lower leg/ankle reveals an apparent physical abnormality or weakness.
The examining man concludes the child will never move like a normal man and says he would not know how to train such a child.
Another figure then decides to take responsibility for the boy's training in combat and in the secret skills of the Shabda-Oud.
uncertainties: The exact identities of the two adult men are not explicitly readable from this page alone.
The precise nature of Aghnar's physical condition is not medically specified; only impaired normal movement is stated.
The final speaker is shown mostly in silhouette, so visual identification is uncertain without surrounding pages.
visual_summary: A large armored or heavily built man examines a newborn held by a dark-haired woman. Close-up panels show the baby's ankle/foot and the adults' worried faces. The baby is lifted and cries while the adults discuss his condition. The final panel shifts to a dark silhouette speaking decisively from below.
